results.name: wide_set_interior_yes_rate
results.description: For sets spanning at least 40, yes-rate for interior targets more than 8 from every example; observed below null means the model over-generalises to the whole interval between widely spread examples.
results.code:
# name: wide_set_interior_yes_rate
# description: For sets spanning at least 40, yes-rate for interior targets more than 8 from every example; observed below null means the model over-generalises to the whole interval between widely spread examples.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(X, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    inr = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    m = ((hi - lo) >= 40) & inr & (dist > 8)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: trial_index_drift
results.description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and rating; observed more negative than null means humans say yes less often as the session goes on, a drift the model lacks.
results.code:
# name: trial_index_drift
# description: Pearson correlation between trial_index and rating; observed more negative than null means humans say yes less often as the session goes on, a drift the model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(X, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    inr = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    ti = df["trial_index"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    if np.std(ti) == 0 or np.std(r) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(ti, r)[0, 1])

results.name: last_digit_gap_mixed_sets
results.description: Among sets with mixed parity (no parity or ends-in rule fits), for non-example targets, yes-rate when target shares its last digit with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means humans generalise by shared last digit more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: last_digit_gap_mixed_sets
# description: Among sets with mixed parity (no parity or ends-in rule fits), for non-example targets, yes-rate when target shares its last digit with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means humans generalise by shared last digit more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(X, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    inr = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    p0 = np.where(valid, X % 2, np.nan)
    mixed = np.nanmin(p0, axis=1) != np.nanmax(p0, axis=1)
    ld = np.any(valid & ((np.nan_to_num(X) % 10) == (t % 10)[:, None]), axis=1)
    base = mixed & (dist > 0)
    a = base & ld; b = base & ~ld
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: parity_gap_within_range
results.description: Among sets whose examples all share one parity, for targets strictly inside the example range (not equal to an example), yes-rate for parity-matching minus mismatching targets; observed above null means humans weight parity more than the model, which lets intervals say yes regardless of parity.
results.code:
# name: parity_gap_within_range
# description: Among sets whose examples all share one parity, for targets strictly inside the example range (not equal to an example), yes-rate for parity-matching minus mismatching targets; observed above null means humans weight parity more than the model, which lets intervals say yes regardless of parity.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    lo = np.nanmin(X, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    inr = (t >= lo) & (t <= hi)
    par = np.nan_to_num(X % 2, nan=-1)
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    p0 = np.where(valid, par, np.nan)
    same = np.nanmin(p0, axis=1) == np.nanmax(p0, axis=1)
    match = (t % 2) == np.nanmin(p0, axis=1)
    base = same & inr & (dist > 0)
    a = base & match; b = base & ~match
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
